title: CLAUDE.md - MOSAIC R Package
text: calc_model_likelihood() computes multi-component log-likelihood: Core: Negative Binomial time-series likelihood cases deaths (weighted MoM dispersion, k_min floor). Shape terms (T-normalized, weight > 0 enables): - Peak timing (Normal LL time differences) - Peak magnitude (log-Normal peak ratios) - Cumulative progression (NB fractions 0.25/0.5/0.75/1.0) - WIS (Weighted Interval Score per Bracher et al. 2021) Assembly: LL = w_cases*NB_cases + w_deaths*NB_deaths + (T/N_peaks)*w_pt*peaks + T*w_cum*cumulative + T*w_wis*WIS shape term weights default 0 (). Non-finite LL returns -Inf.

arrow R package will compile from source # This takes longer but avoids repository configuration issues  # Install Python 3.9+ echo "[5/7] Installing Python 3.9+..." sudo apt-get install -y \   python3 \   python3-pip \   python3-venv \   python3-dev  # Verify Python version PYTHON_VERSION=$(python3 --version 2>&1 | grep -oP '\d+\.\d+' | head -1) PYTHON_MAJOR=$(echo $PYTHON_VERSION | cut -d. -f1) PYTHON_MINOR=$(echo $PYTHON_VERSION | cut -d. -f2)  if [ "$PYTHON_MAJOR" -lt 3 ] || ([ "$PYTHON_MAJOR" -eq 3 ] && [ "$PYTHON_MINOR" -lt 9 ]); then   echo "WARNING: Python $PYTHON_VERSION detected, but >= 3.9 required"   echo "Attempting to install Python 3.9..."   sudo add-apt-repository -y ppa:deadsnakes/ppa   sudo apt-get update   sudo apt-get install -y python3.9 python3.9-venv python3.9-dev   sudo update-alternatives --install /usr/bin/python3 python3 /usr/bin/python3.9 1   echo "Python 3.9 installed and set as default" else   echo "Python $PYTHON_VERSION detected (OK)" fi  # Install critical geospatial R packages first (these often fail) echo "[6/7] Installing critical geospatial R packages..." sudo Rscript -e " options(repos = c(CRAN = 'https://cloud.r-project.org'))  # Install remotes if (!requireNamespace('remotes', quietly = TRUE)) {   install.packages('remotes') }  # Install geospatial packages one by one with error checking cat('Installing sf...
') if (!requireNamespace('sf', quietly = TRUE)) {   install.packages('sf', configure.args = '--with-proj-lib=/usr/lib')   if (!requireNamespace('sf', quietly = TRUE)) {     stop('Failed to install sf package')   } }  cat('Installing terra (version compatible with GEOS 3.8)...
') if (!requireNamespace('terra', quietly = TRUE)) {   # Ubuntu 20.04 has GEOS 3.8, but current terra requires GEOS 3.10+   # Install terra 1.7-71 (last version compatible with GEOS 3.8)   remotes::install_version('terra', version = '1.7.71', repos = 'https://cloud.r-project.org')   if (!requireNamespace('terra', quietly = TRUE)) {     stop('Failed to install terra package')   } }  cat('Installing raster (version compatible with terra 1.7-71)...
') if (!requireNamespace('raster', quietly = TRUE)) {   # Latest raster requires terra >= 1.8.5, but we have terra 1.7-71   # Install raster 3.6-26 (compatible with terra 1.7-71)   remotes::install_version('raster', version = '3.6.26', repos = 'https://cloud.r-project.org')   if (!requireNamespace('raster', quietly = TRUE)) {     stop('Failed to install raster package')   } }  cat('Geospatial packages installed successfully

Rscript -e "MOSAIC::install_dependencies(force = TRUE)"  # Configure R wrapper for Ubuntu 20.04 GLIBCXX compatibility echo "Configuring R wrapper for Ubuntu 20.04 compatibility..." if [ "$OS_VERSION" = "20.04" ]; then   echo "  Creating r-mosaic-R and r-mosaic-Rscript wrappers..."    # Create ~/bin directory   mkdir -p ~/bin    # Create R wrapper script with auto-detection of libstdc++ location   cat > ~/bin/r-mosaic-R <<'EOF' #!/usr/bin/env bash # Find a modern libstdc++ inside common reticulate env locations candidates=(   "$HOME/.virtualenvs/r-mosaic/lib/libstdc++.so.6"   "$HOME/.local/share/r-miniconda/envs/r-mosaic/lib/libstdc++.so.6"   "$HOME/.local/share/r-miniconda/envs/r-reticulate/lib/libstdc++.so.6" ) for f in "${candidates[@]}"; then   export LD_PRELOAD="$HOME/.virtualenvs/r-mosaic/lib/libexpat.so.1${LD_PRELOAD:+:$LD_PRELOAD}" fi # Set R library path to include user library export R_LIBS_USER="$HOME/R/library" [ -x "$HOME/.virtualenvs/r-mosaic/bin/python" ] && export RETICULATE_PYTHON="$HOME/.virtualenvs/r-mosaic/bin/python" exec Rscript "$@" EOF   chmod +x ~/bin/r-mosaic-Rscript   head -1 ~/bin/r-mosaic-Rscript | grep -q '^#!' || { echo "ERROR: ~/bin/r-mosaic-Rscript shebang malformed (not at column 0)"; what: Run a fixed number of simulations for one location
title: Running MOSAIC
code: # Load required packages library(MOSAIC)  MOSAIC::attach_mosaic_env(silent = FALSE)   # Create output directory and set up logging dir_output <- path.expand("~/MOSAIC/output/ETH_fixed") if (!dir.exists(dir_output)) dir.create(dir_output, recursive = TRUE)  set_root_directory("~/MOSAIC")   priors_ETH <- get_location_priors(iso="ETH") config_ETH <- get_location_config(iso="ETH")  control_ETH <- mosaic_control_defaults()  control_ETH$calibration$n_simulations <- 500 control_ETH$calibration$n_iterations <- 2  control_ETH$parallel$enable <- TRUE control_ETH$parallel$n_cores <- parallel::detectCores()-1  control_ETH$targets$ESS_param <- 100 control_ETH$targets$ESS_param_prop <- 0.9 control_ETH$targets$ESS_best <- 50 control_ETH$targets$ESS_method <- 'perplexity'  control_ETH$sampling$sample_tau_i <- FALSE # Travel probability control_ETH$sampling$sample_mobility_gamma <- FALSE   # Gravity model exponent control_ETH$sampling$sample_mobility_omega <- FALSE   # Mobility rate  control_ETH$likelihood$weight_cases <- 1 control_ETH$likelihood$weight_deaths <- 0.05  control_ETH$predictions$n_iter_best <- 30 control_ETH$predictions$n_iter_ensemble <- 5   control_ETH$paths$clean_output <- TRUE control_ETH$io <- mosaic_io_presets("fast")  result_ETH <- run_MOSAIC(      dir_output = dir_output,      config = config_ETH,      priors = priors_ETH,      control = control_ETH,      resume = FALSE )

what: Run the adaptive simulation algorithm for multiple locations
title: Running MOSAIC
code: # Load required packages library(MOSAIC)  MOSAIC::attach_mosaic_env(silent = FALSE)  # Create output directory and set up logging dir_output <- path.expand("~/MOSAIC/output/ETH_KEN") if (!dir.exists(dir_output)) dir.create(dir_output, recursive = TRUE)  set_root_directory("~/MOSAIC")  iso_codes <- c("ETH", "KEN")  priors <- get_location_priors(iso=iso_codes) config <- get_location_config(iso=iso_codes)  control <- mosaic_control_defaults()  control$calibration$n_simulations <- 'auto' control$calibration$n_iterations <- 3 control$calibration$batch_size_adaptive <- 500 control$calibration$min_batches_adaptive <- 5 control$calibration$max_batches_adaptive <- 10 control$calibration$target_r2_adaptive <- 0.95 control$calibration$max_simulations_total <- 1e+06  control$parallel$enable <- TRUE control$parallel$n_cores <- parallel::detectCores()-1  control$targets$ESS_param <- 100 control$targets$ESS_param_prop <- 0.95 control$targets$ESS_best <- 30 control$targets$ESS_method <- 'perplexity'  control$sampling$sample_tau_i <- length(iso_codes) > 1 # Travel probability control$sampling$sample_mobility_gamma <- length(iso_codes) > 1  # Gravity model exponent control$sampling$sample_mobility_omega <- length(iso_codes) > 1  # Mobility rate  control$likelihood$weight_cases <- 1 control$likelihood$weight_deaths <- 0.05  control$predictions$n_iter_best <- 50 control$predictions$n_iter_ensemble <- 10  control$paths$clean_output <- TRUE control$io <- mosaic_io_presets("fast")  control$logging$verbose <- TRUE  result <- run_MOSAIC(      dir_output = dir_output,      config = config,      priors = priors,      control = control,      resume = FALSE )

title: Running simulations
text: MOSAIC includes pre-configured parameter sets different transmission scenarios. Let’s run visualize two key scenarios: epidemic endemic transmission.

title: Running simulations
text: epidemic configuration simulates outbreak dynamics explosive growth patterns typical cholera epidemics.

library(MOSAIC)  # Run epidemic scenario config <- MOSAIC::config_simulation_epidemic  model_epidemic <- run_simulation(config = config, seed = 123, quiet = FALSE)  # Extract time series results (locations x time matrices) cases_epidemic <- as.matrix(model_epidemic$results$reported_cases) deaths_epidemic <- as.matrix(model_epidemic$results$reported_deaths)  # Get metadata locations <- config_simulation_epidemic$location_name n_locations <- length(locations) n_timesteps <- ncol(cases_epidemic)  # Calculate total burden total_cases_epidemic <- sum(cases_epidemic, na.rm = TRUE) total_deaths_epidemic <- sum(deaths_epidemic, na.rm = TRUE)  cat(sprintf("Epidemic Scenario Results:
")) cat(sprintf("  Total cases: %s
", format(total_cases_epidemic, big.mark = ","))) cat(sprintf("  Total deaths: %s
", format(total_deaths_epidemic, big.mark = ","))) cat(sprintf("  Locations: %d
", n_locations)) cat(sprintf("  Time steps: %d
", n_timesteps))  # Plot epidemic time series by location png("figures/running_mosaic_epidemic.png", width = 800, height = 600, res = 120)  colors <- c("#009ADE", "#FF1F5B", "#00CD6C")  # Blue, Pink, Green par(mfrow = c(2, 1), mar = c(3, 4, 3, 1), oma = c(2, 0, 0, 0))  matplot(t(cases_epidemic), type = "l", lty = 1, lwd = 2, col = colors,         xlab = "", ylab = "Reported Cases",         main = "Epidemic Transmission Simulation")  matplot(t(deaths_epidemic), type = "l", lty = 1, lwd = 2, col = colors,         xlab = "Time step", ylab = "Reported Deaths", main = "")  par(fig = c(0, 1, 0, 1), oma = c(0, 0, 0, 0), mar = c(0, 0, 0, 0), new = TRUE) plot(0, 0, type = "n", bty = "n", xaxt = "n", yaxt = "n") legend("bottom", legend = locations, col = colors, lty = 1, lwd = 2,        horiz = TRUE, bty = "n", xpd = TRUE)  dev.off() cat("Saved: figures/running_mosaic_epidemic.png

title: Map infections to suspected and true cholera cases — calc_cases_from_infections
text: Shift-delay model constant \(\rho\): $$\mathbb{E}[C_{\text{true}}(t)] \;=\; \rho\,I_{\text{sym}}(t-\Delta),$$ $$\mathbb{E}[C_{\text{sus}}(t)] \;=\; \frac{\rho}{\chi_t}\,I_{\text{sym}}(t-\Delta),$$ \(\chi_t \(0,1]\) PPV among suspected cases (fraction truly cholera). Epidemic switching rule (optional): $$\chi_t \;=\; \begin{cases} \text{chi\_epidemic}, & \text{} I_{\text{sym}}(t-\Delta)/N(t-\Delta) > \text{epidemic\_threshold},\\ \text{chi\_endemic},  & \text{otherwise.} \end{cases}$$ epidemic_threshold NULL, function uses chi_endemic times (.e., switching bypassed N ignored). delta_t > 0, first delta_t elements outputs NA (earlier infections available map forward). delta_t = 0, outputs aligned one--one infections contain leading NAs.

title: Map infections to suspected and true cholera cases — calc_cases_from_infections
text: Outputs indexed report day \(t\). Values indices \(1:\Delta\) NA depend \(I_{\text{sym}}(t-\Delta)\) start series.

title: Map infections to suspected and true cholera cases — calc_cases_from_infections
code: infections <- c(0, 1, 2, 5, 40, 120, 200, 75, 50, 30, 15, 10, 3, 0, 0) N <- 20000  # 1) No switching: epidemic_threshold = NULL (chi_endemic used everywhere; N ignored) out1 <- calc_cases_from_infections(   infections = infections,   N = NULL,   rho = 0.70,   chi_endemic = 0.50,   chi_epidemic = 0.75,   epidemic_threshold = NULL,   delta_t = 0 ) out1$cases_suspected; out1$cases_true #>  [1]   0.0   1.4   2.8   7.0  56.0 168.0 280.0 105.0  70.0  42.0  21.0  14.0 #> [13]   4.2   0.0   0.0 #>  [1]   0.0   0.7   1.4   3.5  28.0  84.0 140.0  52.5  35.0  21.0  10.5   7.0 #> [13]   2.1   0.0   0.0  # 2) Switching on: use chi_epidemic when infections/N > 15/100,000 out2 <- calc_cases_from_infections(   infections = infections,   N = N,   rho = 0.70,   chi_endemic = 0.50,   chi_epidemic = 0.75,   epidemic_threshold = 15/100000,   delta_t = 2 ) out2$cases_suspected; out2$cases_true #>  [1]         NA         NA   0.000000   1.400000   2.800000   4.666667 #>  [7]  37.333333 112.000000 186.666667  70.000000  46.666667  28.000000 #> [13]  14.000000   9.333333   4.200000 #>  [1]    NA    NA   0.0   0.7   1.4   3.5  28.0  84.0 140.0  52.5  35.0  21.0 #> [13]  10.5   7.0   2.1

title: Calculate comprehensive convergence diagnostics with status indicators — calc_convergence_diagnostics
text: Status indicators calculated using multiplicative thresholds relative targets: "higher better" metrics (ESS, Agreement): PASS: value >= target * pass_threshold WARN: value >= target * warn_threshold < pass_threshold FAIL: value < target * warn_threshold "lower better" metrics (CVw): PASS: value <= target * pass_threshold WARN: value <= target * warn_threshold > pass_threshold FAIL: value > target * warn_threshold Default thresholds metric: ESS_B: pass=0.8 (80%), warn=0.5 (50%) A_B: pass=0.9 (90%), warn=0.7 (70%) CVw_B: pass=1.2 (120%), warn=2.0 (200%) B_size: pass=1.0 (100%), warn=0.5 (50%) Percentile: pass=1.0 (100%), warn=1.5 (150%) Param ESS: pass=1.0 (100%), warn=0.8 (80%)

title: Calculate comprehensive convergence diagnostics with status indicators — calc_convergence_diagnostics
text: overall convergence status determined aggregating individual metric statuses: FAIL: metric status "fail" WARN: failures, least one metric status "warn" PASS: metrics status "pass"

what: Calculate deaths from symptomatic infections with threshold-dependent IFR — calc_deaths_from_infections
title: Calculate deaths from symptomatic infections with threshold-dependent IFR — calc_deaths_from_infections
text: Maps symptomatic infections deaths using infection fatality ratio (IFR) increases epidemic periods incidence exceeds threshold. IFR can also include temporal trend component. Deaths can delayed relative infections account time symptom onset death.

title: Calculate deaths from symptomatic infections with threshold-dependent IFR — calc_deaths_from_infections
code: calc_deaths_from_infections(   infections,   N,   mu_baseline,   mu_slope = 0,   mu_epidemic_factor,   epidemic_threshold,   delta_t = 0 )

title: Calculate deaths from symptomatic infections with threshold-dependent IFR — calc_deaths_from_infections
text: infections Numeric vector new symptomatic infections time one location N Scalar vector population size (can time-varying) mu_baseline Scalar baseline IFR location (0 1) mu_slope Scalar temporal slope factor (default 0 trend) mu_epidemic_factor Scalar proportional increase epidemic (e.g., 0.5 = 50% increase) epidemic_threshold Scalar location-specific threshold (infections/N) epidemic definition delta_t Non-negative integer number days infection--death delay (default 0)

title: Calculate deaths from symptomatic infections with threshold-dependent IFR — calc_deaths_from_infections
text: Numeric vector deaths time step

title: Calculate deaths from symptomatic infections with threshold-dependent IFR — calc_deaths_from_infections
text: time-varying IFR calculated : $$\mu_t = \mu_{baseline} \times (1 + \mu_{slope} \times t) \times (1 + \mu_{epidemic} \times \mathbb{1}_{epidemic})$$ \(\mathbb{1}_{epidemic}\) 1 incidence rate exceeds threshold, 0 otherwise. delta_t > 0, deaths time t result infections time t - delta_t. first delta_t elements output NA since infection data available start time series.

title: Calculate deaths from symptomatic infections with threshold-dependent IFR — calc_deaths_from_infections
code: # Simulate an outbreak infections <- c(10, 20, 50, 100, 80, 40, 20, 10) deaths <- calc_deaths_from_infections(   infections = infections,   N = 100000,   mu_baseline = 0.01,   mu_slope = 0,   mu_epidemic_factor = 0.5,   epidemic_threshold = 30/100000,   delta_t = 0 )  # With temporal trend deaths_trend <- calc_deaths_from_infections(   infections = infections,   N = 100000,   mu_baseline = 0.01,   mu_slope = 0.1,  # 10% increase over time period   mu_epidemic_factor = 0.5,   epidemic_threshold = 30/100000,   delta_t = 0 )  # With 3-day infection-to-death delay deaths_delayed <- calc_deaths_from_infections(   infections = infections,   N = 100000,   mu_baseline = 0.01,   mu_slope = 0,   mu_epidemic_factor = 0.5,   epidemic_threshold = 30/100000,   delta_t = 3 )

title: Compute Diffusion Matrix Based on Gravity Model — calc_diffusion_matrix_pi

title: Compute Diffusion Matrix Based on Gravity Model — calc_diffusion_matrix_pi

title: Compute Diffusion Matrix Based on Gravity Model — calc_diffusion_matrix_pi
text: normalized gravity model following form: $$\pi_{ij} = \frac{N_j^\omega \, d_{ij}^{-\gamma}}{\sum_{j \ne } N_j^\omega \, d_{ij}^{-\gamma}}, \quad \forall \; ,\, j$$ \(d_{ij}\) distance locations \(\) \(j\), \(N_j\) population weight location \(j\). diagonal output matrix set NA, \(\pi_{ij}\) intended used conditionally alongside departure probability \(\tau_i\).

title: Compute Diffusion Matrix Based on Gravity Model — calc_diffusion_matrix_pi

title: Fit Diagnostics: Bias, Shape, and Variance for a Single Observed/Predicted Series — calc_fit_diagnostics
text: Computes structured set fit-quality diagnostics comparing observed daily series model-predicted daily series, decomposed along three independent dimensions: bias (total scale, year, epidemic regime), shape (peak timing, peak magnitude, onset slope, seasonal correlation, timing-normalised shape correlation), variance (coefficient--variation ratio residual autocorrelation). PASS/WARN/FAIL scorecard summarises dimension. metrics engine behind active fit-diagnostic workflow (see diagnose-fit skill run_fit_sandbox()). country-agnostic: takes plain numeric vectors, can unit-tested without running model.

text: observed Numeric vector; observed daily series (NA allowed missing days). predicted Numeric vector; model-predicted daily series, length observed. dates Date vector (coercible) aligned observed/predicted. epidemic_threshold Optional numeric; observed value /day classed epidemic bias split. Default NULL (75th percentile positive observed values). smooth_window Integer; centred running-mean window (days) used peak detection. Default 28. na_rm Logical; drop NA pairs level metrics. Default TRUE.

text: named list elements: bias list: total, by_year (named vector), endemic, epidemic. r2 list: corr, sse, by_year (named vector, corr method). shape list: peak_timing_error_by_year (days; positive = model peaks later), peak_magnitude_ratio_by_year (pred/obs), onset_slope_ratio, seasonal_corr, shape_corr. variance list: cv_ratio (pred CV / obs CV), residual_autocorr_lag7. scorecard named character vector: bias, peak_timing, peak_shape, variance, "PASS"|"WARN"|"FAIL".

title: Fit Diagnostics: Bias, Shape, and Variance for a Single Observed/Predicted Series — calc_fit_diagnostics
text: Diagnose dimension order. Bias addressed first shape variance diagnostics confounded total scale wrong. Reuses calc_model_R2() (corr SSE) calc_bias_ratio() level metrics. endemic/epidemic bias split pragmatic observed-magnitude proxy: days whose observed value epidemic_threshold treated epidemic, rest endemic. epidemic_threshold NULL threshold defaults 75th percentile positive observed values. diagnostic heuristic, model's internal regime classifier.

what: Calculate Kullback-Leibler Divergence Between Two Distributions — calc_kl_divergence
title: Calculate Kullback-Leibler Divergence Between Two Distributions — calc_kl_divergence
text: Computes Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence two probability distributions represented weighted samples. KL divergence measures one probability distribution diverges reference distribution.

title: Calculate Kullback-Leibler Divergence Between Two Distributions — calc_kl_divergence
code: calc_kl_divergence(   samples1,   weights1 = NULL,   samples2,   weights2 = NULL,   n_points = 1000,   eps = 1e-10 )  calculate_kl_divergence(   samples1,   weights1 = NULL,   samples2,   weights2 = NULL,   n_points = 1000,   eps = 1e-10 )

title: Calculate Kullback-Leibler Divergence Between Two Distributions — calc_kl_divergence
text: samples1 Numeric vector samples first distribution (P). weights1 Numeric vector weights samples1. Must length samples1. NULL, uniform weights used. samples2 Numeric vector samples second distribution (Q). weights2 Numeric vector weights samples2. Must length samples2. NULL, uniform weights used. n_points Integer specifying number points kernel density estimation. Higher values provide accurate estimates require computation. Default 1000. eps Numeric value numerical stability. Small positive value added densities avoid log(0). Default 1e-10.

title: Calculate Kullback-Leibler Divergence Between Two Distributions — calc_kl_divergence
text: non-negative numeric value representing KL divergence. Returns 0 distributions identical, larger values indicate greater divergence.

title: Calculate Kullback-Leibler Divergence Between Two Distributions — calc_kl_divergence
text: KL divergence KL(P||Q) calculated : $$KL(P||Q) = \sum_i P(x_i) \log(P(x_i) / Q(x_i))$$ P represents distribution samples1 Q represents distribution samples2. function uses weighted kernel density estimation approximate continuous distributions discrete samples, evaluates KL divergence using numerical integration. Note KL divergence symmetric: KL(P||Q) ≠ KL(Q||P).

title: Calculate Kullback-Leibler Divergence Between Two Distributions — calc_kl_divergence
code: # Example 1: Compare two normal distributions set.seed(123) samples1 <- rnorm(1000, mean = 0, sd = 1) samples2 <- rnorm(1000, mean = 0.5, sd = 1.2) kl_div <- calc_kl_divergence(samples1, NULL, samples2, NULL) print(paste("KL divergence:", round(kl_div, 4))) #> [1] "KL divergence: 0.1338"  # Example 2: Using weighted samples samples1 <- rnorm(500) weights1 <- runif(500, 0.5, 1.5) samples2 <- rnorm(500, mean = 1) weights2 <- runif(500, 0.5, 1.5) kl_div_weighted <- calc_kl_divergence(samples1, weights1, samples2, weights2)  # Example 3: Comparing posterior to prior in Bayesian analysis # prior_samples <- rnorm(1000, mean = 0, sd = 2)  # Prior # posterior_samples <- rnorm(1000, mean = 1, sd = 0.5)  # Posterior # kl_div <- calc_kl_divergence(posterior_samples, NULL, prior_samples, NULL)

FALSE, estimate shape parameters directly observed vector. weights Optional numeric vector non-negative weights, length observed. title: Calculate log-likelihood for Beta-distributed proportions — calc_log_likelihood_beta
text: mean_precision = TRUE, precision parameter \(\phi\) estimated : $$ \phi = \frac{\mu (1 - \mu)}{\text{Var}(Y)} - 1 $$ : $$ \text{shape}_1 = \mu_t \phi, \quad \text{shape}_2 = (1 - \mu_t) \phi $$ mean_precision = FALSE, single global \(\text{shape}_1\), \(\text{shape}_2\) estimated observed vector: $$ \text{shape}_1 = \left( \frac{1 - \mu}{\sigma^2} - \frac{1}{\mu} \right) \mu^2 $$ $$ \text{shape}_2 = \text{shape}_1 \left( \frac{1}{\mu} - 1 \right) $$ total log-likelihood summed across observations, multiplied weights[].

title: Stable log-mean-exp computation — calc_log_mean_exp
text: log-mean-exp vector \(x\) computed : $$ \mathrm{LME}(x) = \max(x) + \log\left(\frac{1}{|x|}\sum_i e^{x_i - \max(x)}\right) $$ numerically stable : maximum value subtracted exponentiation, preventing overflow least one exponentiated term equals 1, preventing underflow Equivalent log(mean(exp(x))) without numerical issues

title: Stable log-mean-exp computation — calc_log_mean_exp
code: # Basic usage x <- c(-100, -101, -99) calc_log_mean_exp(x)  # ≈ -99.59 #> [1] -99.69101  # Compare with naive approach (which would overflow for large negative values) log(mean(exp(x)))     # Same result, but less stable #> [1] -99.69101  # With missing/infinite values calc_log_mean_exp(c(-50, -Inf, -60, NA))  # Returns log-mean-exp of finite values #> [1] -50.6931  # Empty or all non-finite input calc_log_mean_exp(c())           # Returns NA #> [1] NA calc_log_mean_exp(c(-Inf, NA))   # Returns NA #> [1] NA

title: Calculate Effective Sample Size (ESS) — calc_model_ess
text: Numeric scalar: effective sample size.

title: Calculate Effective Sample Size (ESS) — calc_model_ess
text: Two methods available: Kish method (method = "kish"): Uses standard Kish ESS formula: \(\mathrm{ESS} = (\sum w)^2 / \sum w^2\). provides measure much information retained using weighted samples compared unweighted sample size. Perplexity method (method = "perplexity"): Uses exponential entropy: \(\mathrm{ESS} = \exp(-\sum w_i \log w_i)\), weights first normalized sum 1. measures effective number models based entropy weight distribution. Also known perplexity exponential entropy. methods yield values 1 (weight one model) \(n\) (uniform weights), measure slightly different aspects weight concentration. Kish formula commonly used survey sampling, perplexity common information theory model averaging.

title: Calculate Effective Sample Size (ESS) — calc_model_ess
text: Kish, L. (1965). Survey Sampling. Wiley.

title: Calculate Effective Sample Size (ESS) — calc_model_ess

title: Compute Parameter Sensitivity Ranking (R2-HSIC) — calc_model_parameter_sensitivity
text: Computes R2-HSIC (Hilbert-Schmidt Independence Criterion) sampled parameter log-likelihood calibration samples.parquet file. HSIC measures statistical dependence without assuming linearity, monotonicity, independence among inputs, making valid importance-weighted posterior samples parameters correlated (Da Veiga 2015). R2-HSIC index equals zero iff parameter log-likelihood statistically independent (RBF kernel).

text: Converts numeric vector model scores (treated loss-like, .e., lower--better) normalized posterior weights using Gibbs (generalized Bayes) formulation: $$w_m(\eta) = \frac{\exp(-\eta \, x_m)}{\sum_{j=1}^K \exp(-\eta \, x_j)} \,,$$ \(x_m\) loss (information criterion) model \(m\) \(\eta \ge 0\) inverse temperature (sharpness) parameter.

Higher values concentrate weight best models; lower values flatten weights. Typical choices: 0.5 \(\Delta\)AIC (Akaike weights), 1 \(-\log L\). verbose Logical; TRUE, prints brief diagnostics (range x, applied shift, entropy, effective number models). ... Reserved backward compatibility. deprecated argument temperature accepted mapped eta warning.

title: Gibbs-Posterior Model Weights — calc_model_weights_gibbs
text: function agnostic specific form \(x\); smaller values assumed indicate better models. Common choices include: \(x = \Delta \mathrm{AIC}\) \; (use eta = 1/2 recover Akaike weights), \(x = -\log L\) \; (use eta = 1 normalized likelihood weights), Cross-validated losses (e.g., RMSE, MSLE), proper scoring rule. start higher--better score (e.g., log-likelihood), pass x = -score lower--better holds. Numerical stability: implementation subtracts \(\min(x)\) prior exponentiation; shift leaves normalized weights unchanged helps avoid underflow/overflow. Special cases: eta = 0: uniform weights. eta = Inf: hard selection (ties share weight equally). x equal: uniform weights.

Scale/offset logit scale (baseline /). z Numeric \((0,1]\) controlling causal EWMA smoothing; 1 = smoothing. k Numeric integer; time offset days. Positive = forward/right; negative = backward/left. text: Numeric vector \(\tilde\psi^{\star}_t\) (length psi): calibrated, offset, NA-filled, smoothed z<1.

title: Calibrate Daily Suitability on the Logit Scale (vector; optional causal EWMA + time offset + NA filling) — calc_psi_star
text: Offset (index shift, days): \(\psi^{(k)}_t = \psi_{t-k}\). Positive \(k\) shifts series forward/right (delay); negative \(k\) shifts backward/left. Non-integer \(k\) rounded nearest integer. Calibration (odds-space power & scale): $$\psi_t^{\star}=\sigma\!\big(\cdot \mathrm{logit}(\tilde\psi_t)+b\big),\quad \tilde\psi_t=\min\{\max(\psi^{(k)}_t,\varepsilon),\,1-\varepsilon\}$$ \(\text{odds}^\star_t = e^{b}\,(\text{odds}_t)^{}\), \; \(\text{odds}_t=\tilde\psi_t/(1-\tilde\psi_t)\). Optional causal smoothing (look-ahead): $$\tilde\psi^{\star}_t = z\,\psi^{\star}_t + (1-z)\,\tilde\psi^{\star}_{t-1},\quad z\(0,1],\ \tilde\psi^{\star}_1=\psi^{\star}_1.$$ NA filling (calibration, smoothing): Choose via fill_method: "locf" — forward fill (LOCF) backward pass leading gaps. "linear" — linear interpolation interior gaps constant edge extension. values NA shifting, function falls back constant baseline \(\sigma(b)\).

title: Calculate spatial importation hazard — calc_spatial_hazard
text: Computes daily probability least one new infection introduced destination location j day t using gravity‐style coupling infectious prevalence across locations.  formulation adapted Bjørnstad & Grenfell (2008) () folds gravity weights directly prevalence term instead using separate coupling constant, (ii) allows ‑reporting location‐specific parameter tau. Concretely, time t destination j hazard $$\mathcal H_{jt} \,=\, \frac{\beta_{jt}\,S^{\*}_{jt}        \bigl[1-\exp\{-(S^{\*}_{jt}/N_{jt})\,\bar y_{jt}\}\bigr]}       {1+\beta_{jt}\,S^{\*}_{jt}},$$ \(S^{\*}_{jt} = (1-\tau_j)\bigl(S_{jt}+V^{\mathrm{sus}}_{1,jt}+V^{\mathrm{sus}}_{2,jt}\bigr)\) locally susceptible pool (adjusted ‑reporting tau<1). \(\bar y_{jt}\) gravity‑weighted prevalence infection entire metapopulation (including destination): $$\bar y_{jt} = \frac{ (1-\tau_j)(I_{1,jt}+I_{2,jt}) +         \sum_{\neq j}\tau_i\,\pi_{ij}\,(I_{1,}+I_{2,}) }        {\sum_{k} N_{kt} }.$$ Note: specification differs two‑stage form original paper used later work mobility matrix carries full coupling strength.

Used use_epidemic_peaks = FALSE. Weeks cases >= cutoff considered outbreak periods environmental suitability calculation. Default behavior uses value create binary indicator. use_epidemic_peaks Logical. TRUE, uses epidemic peak periods est_epidemic_peaks() define environmental suitability using exact peak_start peak_stop dates. Provides deterministic outbreak detection without modifications lead-periods. Default FALSE backwards compatibility. date_start Start data window. Accepts year (e.g. 2000) date string (e.g. "2000-01-01"); year used filtering. Default "2000-01-01". caps far back panel extends (important AI source supplies pre-2000 reconstructions). Pass NULL auto-detect start case data (one year prior earliest case observation). date_stop End data window (year date string). NULL (default), auto-detected latest raw ENSO data availability. forecast_mode Logical. TRUE, includes variables can support forecasting specified horizon. (v0.30.26 case-dependent epidemic memory spatial-import blocks removed entirely, flag now affects final summary-message text climate-anomaly leading-edge behavior.) Default TRUE. forecast_horizon Numeric. Forecasting horizon months. Variables dependent surveillance data beyond horizon excluded forecast mode. Default 3 months. include_lags Logical. TRUE, includes time-lagged climate variables epidemiologically-informed lag periods specific variable. Default FALSE. include_flood_prob Logical. TRUE (default), imputes continuous emdat_flood_prob column every (iso_code, year, week) row via binomial GAM trained observed emdat_flood_active events (see impute_flood_probability), adds four rolling-window aggregates (emdat_flood_prob_4w_max, emdat_flood_prob_12w_max, emdat_flood_prob_12w_sum, emdat_flood_prob_anom). probability covariates populated historical training forecast windows, downstream LSTM consumes feature definition regimes. v7.4 hazard redesign flag master switch THREE hazard-imputation GAMs: additionally triggers impute_cyclone_probability (adds emdat_cyclone_prob emdat_cyclone_prob_12w_max) impute_drought_probability (adds drought_prob slow integrator drought_prob_26w_mean). GAM gated required-column contract, missing input skips hazard. gam_train_stop Date character ("YYYY-MM-DD") NULL. Passed three hazard imputers (impute_flood_probability, impute_cyclone_probability, impute_drought_probability). non-NULL, hazard GAM FIT rows date <= gam_train_stop predicts every row – leakage-hygiene hook building leak-free per-cutoff panel rolling-origin forecast CV. Default NULL = full-data fit (back-compatible). backfill_case_gaps Logical (default TRUE). Linearly interpolate short interior gaps weekly case series (e.g. holiday non-reporting) suitability target built, via backfill_weekly_case_gaps, missing weeks inside active outbreak stamped false zeros downstream NA->0 sanitiser. backfill_max_weeks Integer (default 2L). Maximum interior gap length (weeks) interpolate; longer gaps left zero-fill. backfill_method Interpolation method passed backfill_weekly_case_gaps (default "linear").

title: Cholera Epidemic Peaks Data — epidemic_peaks
text: Scope: dataset full historical detection record surveillance time series (2010+) pre-trimmed particular simulation window. Consumers score peaks specific config window (e.g. calc_model_likelihood(), Python likelihood port, simulation config builders) must filter [date_start, date_stop] first – otherwise .min(abs(date_seq - peak_date)) silently snaps --window peaks t=1 t=N biases peak-shape likelihood terms. internal helper MOSAIC:::.filter_epidemic_peaks() canonical filter applied build time inside make_config_default.R, runtime inside get_location_config(), defensively inside calc_model_likelihood(). Epidemic peaks identified using following methodology: Time series smoothing 28-day running mean window Local maxima detection 10-day comparison windows Prominence-based filtering (minimum 8\ countries; country-specific overrides ) Minimum peak height threshold 3 smoothed cases (default) Minimum 75-day separation consecutive peaks Peak boundaries defined incidence drops 1/3 peak height Country-specific adjustments applied : Niger (NER): Lower prominence threshold (1.5\ Cameroon (CMR): Adjusted threshold (4\ Ethiopia (ETH): Lower threshold (3\ Manual corrections applied known issues including: Ethiopia 2024: February peak corrected March (sustained outbreak) DRC 2023: Added January peak (filtered due proximity) Nigeria 2024: Added October peak Kenya 2022-2023: Added December 2022, removed June 2023 minor peak Mozambique: Added February 2024 March 2025 peaks Somalia: Added major April 2017 peak 2024-2025 peaks Zambia: Added January 2018 peak Tanzania: Added January 2017 peak

text: function implements constrained residual approach: Method Overview: Sample estimated Beta priors V1, V2, E, , R compartments Calculate S constrained residual: S = 1 - (V1 + V2 + E + + R) Apply constraints: ensure S ≥ min_S_proportion handle -allocation Fit Beta distribution S samples using CI expansion method Return priors-compatible structure metadata Constraint Handling: compartments sum > (1 - min_S_proportion), proportionally scale Ensures S always ≥ min_S_proportion biological realism Maintains mathematical consistency: compartments sum 1 Fallback Behavior: estimated priors unavailable compartment, uses default prior parameters Locations without estimated compartments use independent S prior (Beta(30, 7.5)) Graceful degradation ensures function always returns valid results Uncertainty Propagation: S uncertainty incorporates uncertainty compartments Variance inflation applied using CI expansion method consistent est_initial_* functions Countries high vaccination/immunity naturally get lower certain S estimates

title: Estimate V1/V2 Initial-Condition Beta Priors from OCV Campaign History — est_initial_V1_V2
text: Biological notes: V1/V2 MOSAIC/transmission model administrative compartments (dose received). engine independently splits initial counts immune (Vkimm) susceptible (Vksus) substates via phi_1/phi_2. function therefore multiply phi_1/phi_2 — double-count effectiveness, bug present pre-v0.22.11 implementation. two-dose regimens, R01 attendees return R02 transition V1\(\\)V2 R02 date. Non-returners (R01_doses \(-\) R02_doses, positive) remain V1 omega_1 waning R01 onward. Single-dose Euvichol-S campaigns contribute V1. Blank/unknown vaccine products treated conservatively two-dose (pre-2022 campaigns two-dose Shanchol). Waning model: single exponential. Real OCV waning biphasic (fast decay months 0-12, slower thereafter; see Xu et al. 2024, Bi et al. 2017). Single exponential biases V1/V2 counts upward roughly 10-20% campaigns 2-3 years pre-date_start relative biphasic model. considered acceptable initial-condition purposes; implement biphasic separately needed. Coverage ceiling: vacc_ceiling_frac = 0.70 reflects observed peak OCV coverage published campaigns: DRC Katanga 65% (Abubakar et al. 2018), Bangladesh 75% (Qadri et al. 2015), Haiti 80%+ (Luquero et al. 2014). lower ceiling -captures real high-coverage emergency responses.

title: Estimate Prior Distribution for Environmental Half-Saturation Constant (kappa) — est_kappa_prior
text: function assembles literature table ID50 estimates spanning direct human-volunteer challenge studies (Hornick 1971, Cash 1974, Levine 1981/1988, Tacket 1999), QMRA Beta-Poisson fits (Haas, Rose & Gerba 1999), expert-review summaries (Nelson et al. 2009, Kaper et al. 1995), values adopted convention cholera modelling literature (Codeco 2001, Hartley et al. 2006). source weighted relevance endemic / buffered exposure context relevant sub-Saharan African transmission settings. lognormal fit weighted maximum-likelihood log10 scale. MOSAIC dose-response follows Codeco (2001) Hartley et al. (2006): infection hazard saturating Michaelis-Menten function environmental concentration half-saturation \(\kappa\). Historical cholera models fixed \(\kappa = 10^6\) cells, value traceable Sack (1971) Hornick et al. (1971) unbuffered water-exposure healthy adults. Modern re-analyses buffered-exposure volunteer studies (NaHCO3 neutralisation, representative typical endemic exposure food contaminated drinking water) consistently support lower central estimate \(\sim 10^5\) CFU, substantial -study heterogeneity. Fitting: source contributes point estimate \(\log_{10} \kappa_i\) weight \(w_i\) reflecting evidentiary quality. Weighted mean standard deviation log10 scale converted lognormal meanlog sdlog. resulting prior reconciled fit_lognormal_from_ci() meanlog consistent weighted mode 2.5th / 97.5th percentiles match empirical spread.

title: Estimate Environmental Suitability (psi) for Cholera Transmission — est_suitability
text: lstm_v2_hierarchical_film (default, v0.34) – hierarchical-FiLM LSTM, rolling-origin CV. 3-stack LSTM trunk (128->64->32 units, recurrent dropout) maps weekly covariate window (timesteps=13) shared climate-response latent z. Country/region identity modulates z via hierarchical FiLM: region embedding produces (gamma_r, beta_r) zero-initialized country deviation embedding produces (gamma_c, beta_c), applied z_r = (1+gamma_r) * z + beta_r z_c = (1+gamma_c) * z_r + beta_c. gamma use tanh (gain [0,2], identity init); L2 partial-pool penalty shrinks data-sparse countries toward region. sigmoid head outputs psi [0,1]. Trained BCE loss balanced_uniform sample weights (correcting zero-week imbalance – ~72% -MOSAIC training weeks zero, higher per high-incidence country) plus optional per-row confidence-weight overlay. Training uses expanding-window rolling-origin CV (step validates strictly forward time 4-week embargo, early-stopping records best_epoch); model refit full -sample data median(best_epoch). n_seeds fits averaged logit scale yield prediction (canonical psi column), plus seed-dispersion quantiles (diagnostic , predictive intervals). regime fixes v0.33 random-split temporal leak collapsed --sample forecasts. Defaults pinned B4 fixture; override via arch_control. Honest framing. lstm_v2 converts structurally-collapsed flat psi (Pearson ~0.09, ~3\ directional signal (median cross-country Pearson ~0.22, wide per-cell range large anti-correlated minority – psi can worse climatology countries). strictly dominates incumbent shape; decision-grade forecaster. psi reaches downstream simulation engine TWO channels – fractional deviation (psi - psi_bar)/psi_bar (timing/shape) absolute level (environmental-reservoir decay) – response anchor bias_correct can move outbreak magnitude, just timing. Report per-country spread, just median. default response_var "target_D_rate_per_country_floored" (per-capita, per-country anchor), selected "transmission_intensity" 15-country psi->simulation calibration case-skill comparison: D lifts cases-R2 priority/saturated cluster (COD 0.51->0.73, SOM 0.34->0.82, ETH 0.61->0.80) cost regressions 5 low-burden countries (RWA/MWI/AGO/NAM/SSD), accepted global default. region_map="snf_k5", bias_correct=TRUE; snf_k5 ships unvalidated FiLM region map reverts "csv" beat . lstm_v1_legacy (v0.33, frozen) – shared LSTM, random split + sequential fine-tuning. single 3-stack LSTM (128->64->32) country/region identity (one shared model countries). Trained random 60/40 split across weeks MSE logit-transformed target, followed sequential fine-tuning. Frozen canonical v0.33 settings (tunable; legacy knobs hard-coded internally). Retained reproducibility/rollback. Known limitation: random split places temporally-adjacent weeks sides train/val boundary, --sample forecast collapses amplitude – failure lstm_v2 fixes.

title: Estimate Prior Distribution for Symptomatic Shedding Rate (zeta_1) — est_zeta_1_prior
text: function assembles literature table per-person-per-day shedding anchors constructed stool concentration (\(c\), cells per mL) times time-averaged daily stool volume (\(V\), mL per day) defined severity classes (severe, moderate, mild). severity-weighted pool also constructed using severity_mix argument. weighted lognormal fit maximum-likelihood log10 scale. Assembly equation. literature entry contributes \(\zeta_{1,} = c_i \times V_i\) lower upper bounds taken spread concentration volume anchors severity class. Time-averaged stool volumes used (V_sev = 8, V_mod = 4, V_mild = 0.5 L/day) engine's Poisson update multiplies rate current I_sym compartment, already integrates shedding course via \(\gamma_1\). Peak purging rates (~1 L/h, ~14-24 L/day) treated upper-bound sensitivity rows, central anchor. Severity-weighted pool caveat. default severity mix (0.2 / 0.4 / 0.4) severe class dominates ~94 percent arithmetic \(c_{\mathrm{sev}} = 10^8\) 100x larger \(c_{\mathrm{mild}} = 10^6\). acceptable: surveillance observes severe cases disproportionately, effective \(\zeta_1\) data constrains close severe value anyway. severity_mix argument exposed callers can run sensitivity analyses (e.g. outbreak mix 0.35 / 0.40 / 0.25). Weighted MLE log10 scale. Weighted mean SD log10 scale converted lognormal meanlog sdlog: $$\mu_{\log_{10}} = \frac{\sum w_i \log_{10}(\zeta_{1,})}{\sum w_i}, \quad       \sigma^2_{\log_{10}} = \frac{\sum w_i (\log_{10}(\zeta_{1,}) - \mu_{\log_{10}})^2}{\sum w_i}$$ meanlog = mu_log10 * ln(10) sdlog = sigma_log10 * ln(10). Sensitivity returns. $sensitivity list contains three alternative fits: include_calib (refits MOSAIC calibration posterior row weight 0.25, producing much wider sdlog Frame-B-calibrated value 7 OOM biological-units literature anchors), volume_peak (rescales severe-class V=8 L/day rows V=12 L/day), volume_low (rescales V=6 L/day). Per-day vs per-infection. zeta_1 per-day shedding rate symptomatic infectious period; \(\gamma_1^{-1}\) (~10 d) governs duration. cumulative cells shed per symptomatic infection therefore approximately zeta_1 / gamma_1, per-infection contribution ratio vs asymptomatic zeta_ratio * (gamma_2 / gamma_1) (~5x per-day ratio current gamma priors). comparing prior literature quotes cumulative stool output per infection, apply duration multiplier. Relation documented priors. Earlier MOSAIC-docs narrative states zeta_1 ~ Uniform(10^4, 10^8). range derives Frame-B calibration rescaling superseded lognormal literature-derived prior. new prior's 95\ well stale Uniform upper bound. Primary source notes stored claude/zeta_priors_update/zeta_sources/ (14 PDFs + 32 source notes). See claude/zeta_priors_update/plan_zeta_priors_implementation.md full provenance.

title: Estimate Prior Distribution for the Shedding Ratio (zeta_ratio = zeta_1 / zeta_2) — est_zeta_ratio_prior
text: function produces THREE candidate lognormal fits writes precision-weighted combined prior: () Direct channel: weighted-MLE lognormal literature ratio anchors (Smith 2026 medRxiv, Nelson 2009 paired, Kaper 1995, Harris 2012, Chao 2011, Finger 2018, Righetto 2012, Sugimoto 2014, MOSAIC calibration). (B) Derived channel: paired Monte-Carlo lognormal fitted \(\zeta_1\) / \(\zeta_2\) marginals, paired-bootstrap step shared Nelson 2009 anchor. (C) Combined: precision-weighted (inverse-variance) lognormal combination () (B). written priors_default$parameters_global$zeta_ratio. Direct channel (). Weighted MLE log10 literature ratio anchors direct-ratio table. anchors span ~1.6x (Smith 2026 household per-person-day) ~10^5 (Nelson 2009 paired stool concentrations). spread reflects genuinely different quantities (household transmission probability vs stool concentration ratio) preserved fit's sdlog. Derived channel (B). \(\zeta_1 \sim \mathrm{LN}(\mu_1, \sigma_1^2)\) \(\zeta_2 \sim \mathrm{LN}(\mu_2, \sigma_2^2)\) independent, ratio exactly \(\mathrm{LN}(\mu_1 - \mu_2, \sigma_1^2 + \sigma_2^2)\). derived channel uses analytic closed form directly. Nelson 2009 shared primary source marginals, principle induce positive correlation reduce ratio's variance, correctly propagating requires decomposing marginal's variance Nelson-attributable component residual independent component – subjective attribution well-supported available literature. closed-form variance \(\sigma_1^2 + \sigma_2^2\) therefore conservative upper bound true derived-channel spread. 100,000-draw Monte Carlo sample ratio distribution generated diagnostic figure returned $diagnostics$ratio_sample; enter fit statistics. Combined channel (C). Given direct derived fits \(\mathrm{LN}(\mu_A, \sigma_A^2)\) \(\mathrm{LN}(\mu_B, \sigma_B^2)\), precision-weighted mean log scale $$\mu_C = \frac{\mu_A / \sigma_A^2 + \mu_B / \sigma_B^2}{1/\sigma_A^2 + 1/\sigma_B^2}, \quad \sigma_C = \left(1/\sigma_A^2 + 1/\sigma_B^2\right)^{-1/2}$$ Bayesian posterior log-ratio flat priors channels treated independent normal likelihoods. Smith 2026 dose-response note. Smith et al. 2026 (medRxiv) report odds ratio 0.60 (95 percent CI 0.11-3.23) household transmission asymptomatic vs symptomatic index cases, giving inverse transmission ratio ~1.6. near-linear Hill dose-response regime equal contact patterns compatible low per-person-per-day zeta_ratio. value included weight 0.5 alongside Nelson's 10^5 stool-concentration ratio reader can see tension. fitdistrplus dependency. function import fitdistrplus. diagnostic_candidate_fits = TRUE package loaded via requireNamespace() graceful fallback; follows pattern R/est_initial_R.R:704-710.

code: evaluate_rolling_cv(   predictions,   horizons_months = c(1, 3, 5),   baselines = c("seasonal", "persistence", "persistence_last"),   metrics = c("cases", "deaths"),   trusted_only = TRUE,   embargo_weeks = 0,   ess_min = 0,   min_cells_ci = 5L,   n_boot = 1000L,   seed = 1L )

title: Post-hoc evaluation of a rolling-window forecast-validation artifact — evaluate_rolling_cv
text: predictions run_rolling_cv output directory, path predictions.parquet, predictions data frame . horizons_months Cumulative OOS horizons months (default c(1,3,5)). baselines Baselines skill scores (default c("seasonal","persistence","persistence_last")). metrics Metrics evaluate (default c("cases","deaths")). trusted_only Drop rows observed_source == "AI" (default TRUE). embargo_weeks Channel-specific OOS embargo, weeks, cutoff scoring begins. scalar applies metrics; named vector (e.g. c(cases = 4, deaths = 6)) applies per metric. Default 0. ess_min Minimum importance-weight ESS cell enter summary aggregation. Default 0 (gate ). See Details. min_cells_ci Minimum number finite cells (model, metric, window) group required emit bootstrap CI; CI suppressed (lo = hi = NA) ci_suppressed = TRUE. Default 5. n_boot Bootstrap resamples cells skill CI (default 1000). seed RNG seed bootstrap (default 1). predictions carry model column (ensemble, ensemble_opt, best, medoid), every metric computed reported per model; absent column rows treated single "ensemble" model (back-compatible).

title: Post-hoc evaluation of a rolling-window forecast-validation artifact — evaluate_rolling_cv
text: list : cells Per (cutoff x model x iso x metric x window) metrics + per-baseline mae_skill wis_skill, cell ess ess_ok flag. summary Aggregated across ess_ok cells per (model x metric x window): n_cells_used / n_cells_total, mean/median metric, mean baseline skills bootstrap CI (suppressed fewer min_cells_ci finite cells), plus ess_gated ci_suppressed flags.

title: Post-hoc evaluation of a rolling-window forecast-validation artifact — evaluate_rolling_cv
text: post-hoc companion run_rolling_cv() — harness emits predictions ; judgement (metrics, baselines, skill) lives . Horizons cumulative (\(\le h\) months): \(\le h\) window every OOS point within h months per-metric OOS-scoring origin, computed date cutoff_date (disjoint horizon_bucket label), \(\le\)max-horizon window equals full scored OOS set. window (training fit, \(\le\) cutoff) always reported. Scoring uses trusted observed : rows whose observed_source missing "AI" (trusted_only = TRUE). Channel-specific embargo. embargo_weeks may scalar (metrics) named vector c(cases = 4, deaths = 6). metric OOS scoring start re-derived cutoff_date + embargo_weeks[metric] * 7; OOS rows per-metric boundary scored, independent single segment label baked predictions. Default (0) reproduces prior behavior scoring entire segment == "OOS" block. Baselines, fit per (cutoff, country, metric) observed history. "seasonal" (week--year climatology) primary baseline requires \(\ge 2\) years -sample history; less, seasonal baseline (skill) NA (grand-mean fallback). "persistence" (trailing 4-point mean carried forward) "persistence_last" (single last observed value) secondary nulls. baseline also given 50/95\ quantiles -sample residuals, genuine WIS-skill exists: \(1 - WIS_{model}/WIS_{baseline}\). mae_skill analogous MAE ratio. Positive = model beats baseline; NA baseline (interval) formed. Weight-ESS gate. predictions carry ess column (cutoff calibration's importance-weight ESS, constant per cutoff), cell flagged ess_ok = (!.na(ess) & ess >= ess_min). Cells failing gate remain $cells (flagged) excluded $summary aggregation. ess_min = 0 (default) gate (NA ess still flags ess_ok = FALSE, gate threshold 0 admits finite ess). ess column absent, ess_ok = TRUE cells (back-compat) $summary$ess_gated = FALSE.

title: Fourier Series Model with Two Harmonics (Sine-Cosine Form) — fourier_series_double

what: Estimate Beta Prior for Rho (Care-Seeking Rate) and Save Parameter Data Frame — get_rho_care_seeking_params
title: Estimate Beta Prior for Rho (Care-Seeking Rate) and Save Parameter Data Frame — get_rho_care_seeking_params
text: pool two Wiens strata? Symptomatic cholera MOSAIC's setting spans full severity spectrum (mild watery diarrhea severe rapid dehydration). two Wiens 2025 meta-analytic strata bracket spectrum: General diarrhea (3+ loose/liquid stools): 29.9\ (95\ care-seeking broader population diarrheal episodes, appropriate mild--moderate tail symptomatic cholera (majority cases count). Severe diarrhea + cholera: 58.6\ 22 observations. Represents care-seeking symptoms severe enough flagged "severe" specifically cholera, appropriate severe tail symptomatic cholera. Anchoring severe+cholera stratum ALONE biases rho upward (represents severe tail dominated outbreak-response settings enhanced care-seeking, e.g. Haiti 2010-19 outbreak contributes 50\ ALONE biases rho downward (broader category includes many mild, self-resolving episodes reflect cholera-specific severity). Random-effects pooling two strata produces estimate honestly reflects severity spectrum substantial heterogeneity. include GEMS Nasrin 2013 separate co-anchor? Earlier versions (v0.32.5) pooled GEMS pediatric moderate--severe diarrhea (4 SSA sites, 12 stratum-level estimates) Wiens severe+cholera pooled estimate. pooling three problems: (1) GEMS measures pediatric MSD care-seeking, different population MOSAIC's -ages cholera; (2) 12 GEMS strata vs. 1 Wiens meta-analytic summary upside-dimensionally; (3) Wiens 2025 already includes GEMS-derived data (6 Study IDs tagged GEMS/HUAS), direct GEMS entries partially double-counted source populations. Dropping GEMS using Wiens's two strata directly resolves three. Methodology. Random-effects meta-analysis logit scale (DerSimonian-Laird tau^2) two Wiens strata unit pooling. 95\ pooled mean fit Beta distribution via get_beta_params. Geographic provenance (severe+cholera stratum). 23 underlying studies: 16 SSA, 3 Latin America/Caribbean (mostly Haiti 2010-19), 2 Bangladesh, 1 MENA, 1 South Asia (non-BGD). Predominantly SSA + outbreak settings - regime MOSAIC calibrates.

text: function searches min_size max_size step_size, stopping first size three criteria met simultaneously: ESS >= target_ESS >= target_A CVw <= target_CVw Metrics calculated using Gibbs weighting dynamic temperature: Calculate AIC = -2 * likelihood subset Calculate Delta AIC (relative best subset) Calculate dynamic temperature: effective_range = 4.0 (standard Akaike range) actual_range = range(Delta AIC) temperature = 0.5 * (effective_range / actual_range) Apply Gibbs weighting: weights = exp(-Delta AIC / temperature) / Z Calculate ESS, , CVw Gibbs-weighted samples temperature adapts data's actual Delta AIC range, providing consistent discrimination across different likelihood spreads. size meets criteria, returns results max_size converged=FALSE.

text: separate GAM (folded flood label). Tropical cyclones carry opposite climate signature ordinary precipitation floods: sharp wind spike short, crisply-dated footprint. flood-EM-DAT filter historically dropped 49 tropical-cyclone / surge events, neutered flood GAM's wind smooth. Modeling cyclones wind-led GAM restores signal clean input channel; psi LSTM recombines flood cyclone probabilities downstream (shared cholera-contamination mechanism lives LSTM, label). what: Create a Reusable MOSAIC Parallel Cluster — make_mosaic_cluster
title: Create a Reusable MOSAIC Parallel Cluster — make_mosaic_cluster
text: Creates properly configured parallel cluster use run_MOSAIC. cluster handles one-time setup: library loading, thread safety, root directory propagation. can passed multiple run_MOSAIC calls (e.g. across staged estimation) avoid overhead repeated cluster creation.

title: Create a Reusable MOSAIC Parallel Cluster — make_mosaic_cluster
code: make_mosaic_cluster(   n_cores = parallel::detectCores() - 1L,   type = "PSOCK",   require_root = TRUE )

title: Create a Reusable MOSAIC Parallel Cluster — make_mosaic_cluster
text: n_cores Integer. Number worker processes (default: parallel::detectCores() - 1). Clamped number free R connections smaller, message – see Details. type Character. Cluster type: "PSOCK" (default, platforms) require_root Logical. TRUE (default) root directory must set propagated workers, simulation workers need resolve get_paths(). FALSE allows cluster without one, workers handed explicit paths – render_MOSAIC_figures runs post-hoc finished run directory may MOSAIC tree . "FORK" (Linux/Mac , faster startup).

title: Create a Reusable MOSAIC Parallel Cluster — make_mosaic_cluster
text: cluster object (parallel::makeCluster) ready pass run_MOSAIC(cluster = cl).

title: Create a Reusable MOSAIC Parallel Cluster — make_mosaic_cluster
text: cluster setup includes: Thread environment variables (OMP_NUM_THREADS, MKL_NUM_THREADS, TBB_NUM_THREADS, NUMBA_NUM_THREADS, OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS) set 1 main process worker prevent oversubscription. BLAS threads limited 1 per worker via .mosaic_set_blas_threads(1L). Libraries loaded worker: MOSAIC, arrow. Root directory propagated main process via set_root_directory(). Connection cap. worker holds one R connection. default R build permits 128 connections total, three already taken stdin, stdout stderr, requesting ~126 workers fails inside parallel::makeCluster(). n_cores therefore clamped parallelly::freeConnections() - 2 (two held back worker parquet /O) message reports clamp. R 4.4.0 later accept --max-connections=N 4096 raise ceiling. caller responsible stopping cluster done: parallel::stopCluster(cl). returned object also carries "mosaic_worker_pids" attribute recorded creation, run_MOSAIC() uses reap worker survives stopCluster() – see ?.mosaic_stop_cluster.

title: Create a Reusable MOSAIC Parallel Cluster — make_mosaic_cluster
code: if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ library(MOSAIC) set_root_directory("~/MOSAIC")  # Create cluster once cl <- make_mosaic_cluster(n_cores = 8)  # Use across multiple calibration stages result_s1 <- run_MOSAIC(config, priors, "./stage_1", control, cluster = cl) result_s2 <- run_MOSAIC(config, priors_s2, "./stage_2", control, cluster = cl)  # Clean up parallel::stopCluster(cl) } # }

title: Create a Simulation Configuration File — make_simulation_config
text: output_file_path character string representing full file path output file. Must .json, .json.gz, .h5, .hdf5, .h5.gz, .yaml, .yaml.gz extension. NULL, file written parameters returned. seed Integer scalar giving random seed value simulation run. date_start Start date simulation period "YYYY-MM-DD" format. provided character string, converted Date object. date_stop End date simulation period "YYYY-MM-DD" format. provided character string, converted Date object. location_name character vector giving names metapopulation location. order names must match used initial population vectors. N_j_initial named numeric integer vector length equal location_name giving total initial population size location. Note total population size must sum model compartments. S_j_initial named numeric integer vector length equal location_name giving starting number susceptible individuals location. Names must match location_name. E_j_initial named numeric integer vector length equal location_name giving starting number exposed individuals location. Names must match location_name. I_j_initial named numeric integer vector length equal location_name giving starting number infected individuals location. Names must match location_name. R_j_initial named numeric integer vector length equal location_name giving starting number recovered individuals location. Names must match location_name. V1_j_initial named numeric integer vector length equal location_name giving starting number individuals vaccine compartment V1 location. Names must match location_name. V2_j_initial named numeric integer vector length equal location_name giving starting number individuals vaccine compartment V2 location. Names must match location_name. prop_S_initial Optional. named numeric vector length equal location_name giving starting proportion susceptible individuals location. Values must [0,1]. Names must match location_name. proportion fields provided analysis convenience required transmission model. prop_E_initial Optional. named numeric vector length equal location_name giving starting proportion exposed individuals location. Values must [0,1]. Names must match location_name. prop_I_initial Optional. named numeric vector length equal location_name giving starting proportion infected individuals location. Values must [0,1]. Names must match location_name. prop_R_initial Optional. named numeric vector length equal location_name giving starting proportion recovered individuals location. Values must [0,1]. Names must match location_name. prop_V1_initial Optional. named numeric vector length equal location_name giving starting proportion individuals vaccine compartment V1 location. Values must [0,1]. Names must match location_name. prop_V2_initial Optional. named numeric vector length equal location_name giving starting proportion individuals vaccine compartment V2 location. Values must [0,1]. Names must match location_name. b_jt matrix birth rates rows equal length(location_name) columns equal daily sequence date_start date_stop. d_jt matrix mortality rates rows equal length(location_name) columns equal daily sequence date_start date_stop. nu_1_jt matrix first-dose OCV vaccinations location time step. nu_2_jt matrix second-dose OCV vaccinations location time step. phi_1 Effectiveness one dose OCV (numeric [0, 1]). phi_2 Effectiveness two doses OCV (numeric [0, 1]). omega_1 Waning immunity rate one dose (numeric >= 0). omega_2 Waning immunity rate two doses (numeric >= 0). nu_jt_sources Character vector compartment names eligible first-dose vaccination (default c("S", "E", "Isym", "Iasym", "R")). Must non-empty subset c("S", "E", "Isym", "Iasym", "R"). Passed laser-cholera v0.12+ draws first doses proportionally listed compartments. iota Incubation rate E -> (numeric > 0, per day). Note rate, period – prior median ~0.71/day. engine uses iota * E flow E. gamma_1 Symptomatic shedding-duration rate I_sym -> R (numeric >= 0, per day; "severe / symptomatic" branch). gamma_2 Asymptomatic shedding-duration rate I_asym -> R (numeric >= 0, per day; "mild / asymptomatic" branch). epsilon Natural-infection immunity waning rate R -> S (numeric >= 0, per day). Distinct vaccine waning (omega_1, omega_2). mu_jt matrix time-varying probabilities mortality due infection, rows equal length(location_name) columns equal length(t). values must numeric 0 1. mu_j_baseline provided IFR parameters, mu_jt can generated using calc_deaths_from_infections(). mu_j_baseline Baseline infection fatality ratio threshold-dependent IFR model. Numeric vector length(location_name). Values must [0, 1]. mu_j_slope Temporal trend baseline IFR (proportion change simulation period). Numeric vector length(location_name). Default 0 (temporal trend). mu_j_epidemic_factor Proportional increase IFR epidemic periods (e.g., 0.5 = 50% increase). Numeric vector length(location_name). Must >= 0. rho Care-seeking rate: probability symptomatic individual presents surveillance (numeric [0, 1]). reporting fraction sigma – upstream care-seeking step surveillance cascade. rho_deaths Death detection rate: probability true cholera death captured surveillance (numeric [0, 1] NULL). Consumed engine produce reported_deaths (originally laser-cholera#49; pure-R engine implements rule). sigma Proportion infections symptomatic (numeric [0, 1]). chi_endemic Positive predictive value among suspected cases endemic periods (numeric (0, 1]). chi_epidemic Positive predictive value among suspected cases epidemic periods (numeric (0, 1]). epidemic_threshold Isym/N point prevalence threshold epidemic regime activation. Used case reporting IFR threshold models. Numeric scalar length-n vector [0, 1]. delta_reporting_cases Symptom-onset--surveillance reporting delay days (non-negative integer). infection--report – incubation handled separately E compartment iota. delta_reporting_deaths Symptom-onset--death-report delay days (non-negative integer). longitude numeric vector longitudes location. Must length location_name. latitude numeric vector latitudes location. Must length location_name. mobility_omega Exponent weight destination population gravity mobility model. Must numeric ≥ 0. mobility_gamma Exponent weight distance decay gravity mobility model. Must numeric ≥ 0. tau_i Departure probability origin location (numeric vector length(location_name) [0, 1]). beta_j0_tot Total baseline transmission rate (human + environmental). Optional numeric vector length(location_name). provided p_beta, used derive beta_j0_hum beta_j0_env. p_beta Proportion total transmission human--human (0-1). Optional numeric vector length(location_name). provided beta_j0_tot, used derive beta_j0_hum beta_j0_env. beta_j0_hum Baseline human--human transmission rate (numeric vector length(location_name)). beta_j0_tot p_beta provided, validated beta_j0_tot * p_beta. a_1_j Vector sine amplitude coefficients (1st harmonic) location. Numeric, length = length(location_name). a_2_j Vector sine amplitude coefficients (2nd harmonic) location. Numeric, length = length(location_name). b_1_j Vector cosine amplitude coefficients (1st harmonic) location. Numeric, length = length(location_name). b_2_j Vector cosine amplitude coefficients (2nd harmonic) location. Numeric, length = length(location_name). p Period seasonal forcing function. Scalar numeric > 0. Default 365 daily annual seasonality. alpha_1 FOI mixing exponent applied infectious term (/N) (numeric (0, 1]; 1 = well-mixed contacts). Dual-mode (laser-cholera v0.16.0+): scalar applied uniformly across patches, per-location vector length length(location_name). alpha_2 Exponent N_jt FOI denominator (numeric [0, 1]). alpha_2 = 1 frequency-dependent transmission (FOI proportional /N); alpha_2 = 0 density-dependent (FOI proportional ). Dual-mode: scalar per-location vector length length(location_name). beta_j0_env Baseline environment--human transmission rate (numeric vector length(location_name)). beta_j0_tot p_beta provided, validated beta_j0_tot * (1 - p_beta). theta_j Proportion adequate WASH (numeric vector length(location_name) [0, 1]). psi_jt Matrix environmental suitability values (matrix rows = length(location_name) columns equal daily sequence date_start date_stop). psi_star_a Shape/gain parameter logit calibration psi_jt (numeric vector length(location_name) > 0). Values > 1 sharpen peaks, values < 1 flatten peaks. Default 1.0 (transformation). psi_star_b Scale/offset parameter logit calibration psi_jt (numeric vector length(location_name)). Shifts baseline /logit scale. Default 0.0 (offset). psi_star_z Smoothing weight causal EWMA calibrated psi_jt (numeric vector length(location_name) (0,1]). 1.0 = smoothing, < 1.0 = apply smoothing. Default 1.0 (smoothing). psi_star_k Time offset days psi_jt calibration (numeric vector length(location_name)). Positive values = forward/delay, negative values = backward/advance. Default 0.0 (offset). zeta_1 Shedding rate (numeric > 0). zeta_2 Asymptomatic shedding rate (numeric > 0). Derived sample_parameters() zeta_1 / zeta_ratio. kappa Concentration required 50% infection (numeric > 0). decay_days_short Time constant (days) short-term survival V. cholerae environment. Must > 0 < decay_days_long. decay_days_long Time constant (days) long-term survival V. cholerae environment. Must > 0 > decay_days_short. decay_shape_1 First shape parameter beta distribution controlling environmental suitability maps decay rate V. cholerae environment. Must numeric > 0. decay_shape_2 Second shape parameter beta distribution controlling environmental suitability maps decay rate V. cholerae environment. Must numeric > 0. reported_cases Matrix daily reported cholera cases. Must integer. NA allowed. nrow=length(location_name), ncol=length(t). reported_deaths Matrix daily reported cholera deaths. Must integer. NA allowed. nrow=length(location_name), ncol=length(t). epidemic_peaks Optional data.frame observed epidemic peaks consumed peak-timing / peak-magnitude shape terms calc_model_likelihood() (R Python port laser-cholera). Must contain two character columns: iso_code (matching entries location_name) peak_date (ISO YYYY-MM-DD strings parseable .Date). NULL allowed; NULL peak shape terms contribute 0 likelihood. sigfigs Integer; number significant figures round numeric values . Default 4.

what: Build Complete MOSAIC Control Structure — mosaic_control_defaults
title: Build Complete MOSAIC Control Structure — mosaic_control_defaults
text: Creates complete control structure run_mosaic(). primary interface configuring MOSAIC execution settings, consolidating calibration strategy, parameter sampling, parallelization, output options. Parameters organized workflow order: calibration: run (simulations, iterations, batch sizes) sampling: sample (parameters vary) likelihood: score model fit (likelihood components weights) targets: stop (ESS convergence thresholds) parallel: Infrastructure (cores, cluster type) io: Output format (file format, compression) paths: File management (output directories, plots)

title: Build Complete MOSAIC Control Structure — mosaic_control_defaults
text: calibration List calibration settings. Default : n_simulations: NULL auto mode, integer fixed mode n_iterations: Number stochastic engine iterations per parameter set (default: 3L) max_simulations_total: Maximum total simulations across phases (default: 100000L) batch_size_adaptive: Simulations per batch Phase 1 adaptive calibration (default: 500L) min_batches_adaptive: Minimum Phase 1 batches convergence check (default: 5L) max_batches_adaptive: Maximum Phase 1 batches (default: 8L) max_batch_predictive: Cap Phase 2 predictive batch (default: 10000L) max_batches_predictive: Maximum Phase 2 predictive batches (default: 10L) target_r2_adaptive: ESS regression R-squared target Phase 1 convergence (default: 0.90) sampling List parameter sampling flags (sample). Default : sample_tau_i: Sample transmission rate (default: TRUE) sample_mobility_gamma: Sample mobility gamma (default: TRUE) sample_mobility_omega: Sample mobility omega (default: TRUE) sample_mu_j: Sample recovery rate (default: TRUE) sample_iota: Sample importation rate (default: TRUE) sample_gamma_2: Sample second dose efficacy (default: TRUE) sample_alpha_1: Sample within-metapop population mixing exponent (default: TRUE) sample_alpha_2: Sample frequency-dependence degree (default: FALSE; pinned, weakly identified) ... (see mosaic_control_defaults() complete list 38 parameters) likelihood List likelihood calculation settings (score model fit). Default : weight_cases: Weight cases vs deaths (default: 1.0) weight_deaths: Weight deaths vs cases (default: 1.0) weight_wis: WIS regularizer weight (default: 0, try 0.10) ... (see mosaic_control_defaults() complete list) targets List convergence targets (stop). Default : ESS_param: Target ESS per parameter (default: 100) ESS_param_prop: Proportion parameters meeting ESS (default: 0.95) ESS_best: Target subset size ESS within subset (default: 100). A_best: Target agreement index (default: 0.70). Lower values allow top sims dominate. CVw_best: Target CV weights (default: 1.0). Higher values permit sharper discrimination. percentile_min: Minimum percentile best subset search (default: 0.001) ESS_method: ESS calculation method, "kish" "perplexity" (default: "perplexity") predictions List prediction generation settings. Default : n_iter_ensemble: Stochastic runs per posterior parameter set weighted ensemble (default: 10L). Total ensemble sims = N parameter sets x n_iter_ensemble. n_iter_best: Stochastic runs medoid single-config prediction plots (default: 100L). Applied identically models. runs execute internal PSOCK cluster parallel$enable = TRUE. optimize_subset: Logical; TRUE, post-ensemble optimizer (MAE / WIS / R^2+bias) refines best subset used posteriors.json, posterior_quantiles.csv, ensemble object driving downstream plots metrics. tier-selected subset preserved is_best_subset / weight_best columns samples.parquet provenance; optimized selection written new is_best_subset_opt / weight_best_opt columns. FALSE (default), tier-selected subset canonical _opt columns written. Statistical note: enabling flag yields posterior conditioned ensemble predictive performance (MAE / WIS / R^2+bias training data) rather pure likelihood-weighted posterior. optimize_min_n: Minimum subset size optimizer may select (default 30L, raised 4L guard KDE degeneracy posteriors.json). optimize_objective: Objective function, "mae" (default), "r2_bias", "wis". optimize_stride: Integer >= 1 (default 3L). 1L evaluates every candidate subset size min_n:max_n (exhaustive, bit-identical historical search). > 1L runs coarse--refine search evaluates strided grid first refines around best point. default 3L gives roughly 3x speedup negligible accuracy cost smooth score(N) curve (re-examines +/- 3 window around coarse winner); raise (5L/10L/25L) speed, set 1L force exhaustive search. Note may select slightly different optimal_n exhaustive records evaluated N's diagnostics table. (optimize_ensemble_subset function's stride default remains 1L preserve bit-identicality.) central_method: Ensemble central tendency, "median" (default; lower calibration bias) "mean" (unbiased expected counts, never collapses sparse deaths, unmasks implied-CFR bias). Scalar per-channel c(cases=, deaths=). Governs prediction trajectory + plots, canonical *_ensemble R^2/bias metrics, medoid target, subset-selection objective consistently. number parameter sets ensemble determined best subset (sims non-zero importance weights). weights List importance-weight settings. Default : floor: Minimum weight prevent underflow (default: 1e-15). iqr_multiplier: Tukey IQR outlier-detection multiplier (default: 1.5; use 3.0 extreme outliers ). parallel List parallelization settings (infrastructure). Default : enable: Enable parallel execution (default: FALSE) n_cores: Number simulation worker processes (default: 1L) type: Cluster type, "PSOCK" "FORK" (default: "PSOCK") progress: Show progress bar (default: TRUE) io List /O settings (output format). Default : format: Output format, "parquet" "csv" (default: "parquet") compression: Compression algorithm (default: "zstd") compression_level: Compression level (default: 3L) persist_ensemble_arrays: Retain dense 4-D cases_array/deaths_array persisted ensemble RDS files (ensemble_candidate.rds, ensemble_optimized.rds, subset_opt.rds, medoid_ensemble.rds). Default FALSE strips arrays save time -disk artifacts small (~tens KB); every light field (central tendencies, envelopes, weights, seeds, obs, metadata) preserved standard consumers (plotting, OCV, rolling CV) work unchanged. Set TRUE re-analysable raw archive (e.g. re-running subset optimization R_eff posterior-resimulation CI path saved file). -memory object used run never affected (default: FALSE). paths List path output settings (file management). Default : clean_output: Remove output directory exists (default: FALSE) plots: Generate diagnostic plots (default: TRUE) logging List logging settings. Default : verbose: Enable detailed progress messages sub-functions (default: FALSE).

title: Build Complete MOSAIC Control Structure — mosaic_control_defaults
text: complete control list suitable passing run_mosaic().

title: Build Complete MOSAIC Control Structure — mosaic_control_defaults
code: # Default control settings ctrl <- mosaic_control_defaults()  # Quick parallel run with 8 cores ctrl <- mosaic_control_defaults(   parallel = list(enable = TRUE, n_cores = 8) )  # Fixed mode with 5000 simulations, 5 iterations each ctrl <- mosaic_control_defaults(   calibration = list(     n_simulations = 5000,     n_iterations = 5   ) )  # Auto mode with custom settings ctrl <- mosaic_control_defaults(   calibration = list(     n_simulations = NULL,  # NULL = auto mode     n_iterations = 3,     max_simulations_total = 50000,     batch_size_adaptive = 1000   ),   parallel = list(enable = TRUE, n_cores = 16) )  # Only sample specific parameters ctrl <- mosaic_control_defaults(   sampling = list(     sample_tau_i = TRUE,     sample_mobility_gamma = FALSE,     sample_mobility_omega = FALSE,     sample_mu_j_baseline = TRUE,     sample_iota = FALSE,     sample_gamma_2 = FALSE,     sample_alpha_1 = FALSE   ) )  # Enable WIS regularizer and peak timing ctrl <- mosaic_control_defaults(   likelihood = list(     weight_wis = 0.10,     weight_peak_timing = 0.25   ) )  # Use perplexity method for ESS calculations ctrl <- mosaic_control_defaults(   targets = list(ESS_method = "perplexity") )  # Full workflow configuration (demonstrates logical order) ctrl <- mosaic_control_defaults(   calibration = list(n_simulations = NULL, n_iterations = 3),      # How to run   sampling = list(sample_tau_i = TRUE, sample_mu_j_baseline = TRUE), # What to sample   likelihood = list(weight_wis = 0.10, weight_cases = 1.0),        # How to score   targets = list(ESS_param = 100, ESS_param_prop = 0.95),          # When to stop   parallel = list(enable = TRUE, n_cores = 16),                    # Infrastructure   io = mosaic_io_presets("default"),                               # Output format   paths = list(clean_output = FALSE, plots = TRUE)                 # File management )
